verses.text: The LORD's message came to me:
"Son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre.
Say to Tyre, the city at the gateway to the sea, trader to the peoples of many coastlands, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Tyre, you have said, "I am perfect in beauty."
Your borders are in the heart of the sea. Your builders made your beauty perfect.
They made all your planks from pine trees from Senir. They took a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you.
They made your oars from oaks of Bashan. They made your deck from cypress wood from the coasts of Cyprus, inlaid with ivory.
Your sail was made of fine embroidered linen from Egypt, and it served as your flag. Your awnings were blue and purple cloth from the coasts of Elishah.
People from Sidon and Arvad were your rowers. Your own skilled men, Tyre, were your sailors.
Experienced craftsmen from Gebal were on board to repair your seams. All the ships of the sea and their sailors came to trade with you.
Men from Persia, Lud, and Put served as soldiers in your army. They hung their shields and helmets on your walls, bringing you splendor.
Men from Arvad and from your own army guarded your walls on every side. Brave men were in your towers. They hung their shields around your walls, making your beauty perfect.
Tarshish traded with you because of your great wealth of goods. They exchanged silver, iron, tin, and lead for your merchandise.
Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded with you. They exchanged slaves and bronze objects for your goods.
The people of Beth Togarmah exchanged horses, war horses, and mules for your merchandise.
The people of Dedan traded with you, and many coastlands were your customers. They paid you with ivory tusks and ebony.
Aram traded with you because of your many products. They exchanged turquoise, purple cloth, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies for your merchandise.
Judah and the land of Israel traded with you. They exchanged wheat from Minnith, cakes, honey, olive oil, and healing balm for your goods.
Damascus traded with you because of your many products and great wealth of goods. They paid with wine from Helbon and white wool.
Vedan and Greece from Uzal exchanged yarn for your merchandise. Wrought iron, cassia, and sweet cane were among your goods.
Dedan traded with you in saddle blankets for riding.
Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were your customers. They traded with you in lambs, rams, and goats.
Merchants from Sheba and Raamah traded with you. They exchanged the finest spices, all kinds of precious stones, and gold for your merchandise.
Haran, Canneh, Eden, and the merchants of Sheba, Asshur, and Kilmad traded with you.
In your markets they traded fine clothing, blue cloth, embroidered work, and multicolored rugs tied with strong cords.
The ships of Tarshish carried your goods. You were filled with heavy cargo in the heart of the sea.
Your rowers took you out into the deep waters. But the east wind will smash you in the heart of the sea.

Your wealth, your goods, your merchandise, your sailors, your crew, your ship repairers, your merchants, all your soldiers, and everyone else on board will sink into the heart of the sea on the day of your shipwreck.
The shorelands will shake when your sailors cry out.
Everyone who handles the oars will abandon their ships. The sailors and all the crews will stand on the shore.
They will raise their voices and cry bitterly over you. They will throw dust on their heads and roll in ashes.
They will shave their heads because of you and put on sackcloth. They will weep over you with bitter grief and mourning.
As they wail and mourn over you, they will sing a funeral song about you: "Who was ever like Tyre, now silenced in the middle of the sea?"
When your goods went out across the seas, you satisfied many nations. With your great wealth and merchandise you made the kings of the earth rich.
Now you are shattered by the sea, in the depths of the waters. Your goods and all your crew have sunk with you.
Everyone who lives on the coastlands is shocked at what has happened to you. Their kings shudder with horror, and their faces are troubled.
The merchants among the nations hiss at you. You have come to a terrible end and will be no more.'"
